title: 水龙吟·夜来风雨匆匆
title_en: To the Tune of Shui Long Yin: Wind and Rain Rushed Through the Night
author: 程垓

form.zh: 词·水龙吟（双调一百零二字）
form.en: ci lyric to the tune Shui Long Yin (two stanzas, 102 characters)

text_note.zh: 这里用通行本。资料库原文“愁多怨极”作“愁多愁极”，“柳困桃慵”作“柳困花慵”，“拚醉”作“拼醉”（机器转简体时把“拚”换成了“拼”）。
text_note.en: This follows the common text. The database has "chóu duō chóu jí" for "chóu duō yuàn jí", "liǔ kùn huā yōng" for "liǔ kùn táo yōng", and a different character for pàn in "pàn zuì" (the machine conversion to simplified characters swapped it).

readings.zh: 拚：这里读 pàn，意思是豁出去、不顾一切。有的书也读 pīn。
readings.en: This character is read pàn here, meaning "to give everything, not hold back". Some books read it pīn.

glosses.zh: 夜来：昨天夜里。
glosses.en: yè lái: last night.

glosses.zh: 匆匆：急急忙忙，来得快去得快。
glosses.en: cōng cōng: in a rush, coming and going fast.

glosses.zh: 故园：老家的园子。
glosses.en: gù yuán: the garden back home.

glosses.zh: 花无几：花剩下没有多少了。
glosses.en: huā wú jǐ: hardly any flowers are left.

glosses.zh: 愁多怨极：忧愁很多，怨恨到了极点。
glosses.en: chóu duō yuàn jí: so much sorrow, so much bitterness.

glosses.zh: 等闲：随随便便，轻易地。
glosses.en: děng xián: carelessly, too easily.

glosses.zh: 孤负：就是“辜负”，对不起别人的好意。
glosses.en: gū fù: to let down, to waste someone's kindness.

glosses.zh: 芳意：花草带来的春天的美意。
glosses.en: fāng yì: the gift of spring that the flowers bring.

glosses.zh: 柳困桃慵：柳树像困倦了，桃花像懒洋洋的。慵，懒。
glosses.en: liǔ kùn táo yōng: the willows look sleepy and the peach blossoms look lazy. Yōng means lazy.

glosses.zh: 杏青梅小：杏子还青，梅子还小。花已经落了，结出了小果子。
glosses.en: xìng qīng méi xiǎo: the apricots are still green and the plums still small. The flowers are gone and little fruits have come.

glosses.zh: 容易：轻易、随便。这里说春天对人随随便便，说走就走。
glosses.en: róng yì: lightly, without care. Here it means spring treats people lightly and leaves when it likes.

glosses.zh: 算：想来，算起来。
glosses.en: suàn: when you think about it.

glosses.zh: 元只是：原来只是。元，同“原”。
glosses.en: yuán zhǐ shì: in the end it is only. Yuán here means "originally".

glosses.zh: 憔悴：又瘦又没精神的样子。
glosses.en: qiáo cuì: thin, worn out and tired-looking.

glosses.zh: 回首：回头看，回想。
glosses.en: huí shǒu: to look back, to remember.

glosses.zh: 池南旧事：当年在池塘南边发生的事。具体是什么事，词里没有说。
glosses.en: chí nán jiù shì: things that happened long ago south of the pond. The lyric does not say what they were.

glosses.zh: 星星：一般解作头发花白，像点点星星。一说指往事零零碎碎。
glosses.en: xīng xīng: usually read as hair turning grey in spots, like little stars. Another reading: the old memories are scattered bits.

glosses.zh: 不堪重记：受不了再去回想。
glosses.en: bù kān chóng jì: cannot bear to remember again.

glosses.zh: 但有：只有。
glosses.en: dàn yǒu: there is only.

glosses.zh: 伤时：为时光流逝而伤心。
glosses.en: shāng shí: grieving over time slipping away.

glosses.zh: 清泪：清清的眼泪。
glosses.en: qīng lèi: clear tears.

glosses.zh: 逢花瘦：遇上花儿凋零、变得稀少。
glosses.en: féng huā shòu: to meet the flowers when they are thin and fading.

glosses.zh: 风味：兴致、情趣。老来风味，就是人老了以后的兴致。
glosses.en: fēng wèi: zest, the taste for fun. Lǎo lái fēng wèi is the zest one has left in old age.

glosses.zh: 繁红乱处：红花开得又多又乱的地方。
glosses.en: fán hóng luàn chù: where red flowers bloom thick and wild.

glosses.zh: 留云借月：把云留住，把月借来，意思是想办法留住美好的时光。这个说法出自北宋朱敦儒的词。
glosses.en: liú yún jiè yuè: to keep the clouds and borrow the moon, that is, to hold on to the good time somehow. The phrase comes from a lyric by Zhu Dunru of the Northern Song.

glosses.zh: 拚醉：豁出去喝个大醉。
glosses.en: pàn zuì: to drink until drunk, holding nothing back.

translation.zh: 昨夜风雨来得急急忙忙。
translation.en: Last night wind and rain rushed through.

translation.zh: 老家园子里的花，一定没剩下几朵了。
translation.en: In the garden back home, surely few flowers are left.

translation.zh: 忧愁太多，怨恨到了极点，
translation.en: With too much sorrow and bitterness,

translation.zh: 我随随便便就辜负了
translation.en: I carelessly let slip

translation.zh: 这一整年春天的美意。
translation.en: a whole year's gift of spring.

translation.zh: 柳树困倦，桃花慵懒，
translation.en: The willows are sleepy, the peach blossoms lazy,

translation.zh: 杏子还青，梅子还小，
translation.en: the apricots still green, the plums still small.

translation.zh: 春天对人真是随随便便，说走就走。
translation.en: Spring treats people so lightly and simply leaves.

translation.zh: 想来，即使美好的春天一直都在，
translation.en: Even if fair spring stayed forever,

translation.zh: 美丽的花一直都能看到，
translation.en: and lovely flowers could always be seen,

translation.zh: 原来只是人自己一天天憔悴了。
translation.en: it is only that people grow worn and tired.

translation.zh: 回想当年池塘南边的往事，
translation.en: I look back on the old days south of the pond.

translation.zh: 可恨头发已经花白，受不了再去回想。
translation.en: Sadly my hair is grey, and I cannot bear to remember again.

translation.zh: 如今我只剩下
translation.en: Now all I have left

translation.zh: 一双看花的老眼，
translation.en: are old eyes that look at flowers,

translation.zh: 和为时光伤心流下的清泪。
translation.en: and clear tears shed for passing time.

translation.zh: 我不怕遇上花儿凋零稀少，
translation.en: I do not fear meeting flowers that are thin and fading.

translation.zh: 只怕人老了以后没有了兴致。
translation.en: I only fear losing my zest as I grow old.

translation.zh: 等到红花开得最繁最乱的时候，
translation.en: When the red flowers bloom thick and wild,

translation.zh: 我要留住白云，借来明月，
translation.en: I will keep the clouds and borrow the moon,

translation.zh: 也一定要豁出去喝个大醉。
translation.en: and I must drink till I am drunk, holding nothing back.

background.zh: 这首词写在暮春时节，一场夜里的风雨之后。词人想到老家园子里的花大概都被打落了，又想到自己一年来只顾发愁，没好好赏春。它具体写于哪一年、在什么地方，现在不清楚。词里的“池南旧事”应该是词人年轻时的一段往事，但词里没有说明是什么事。
background.en: This lyric was written in late spring, after a night of wind and rain. The poet thinks the flowers in his garden back home must have been knocked down. He also thinks that he spent the whole year worrying and never really enjoyed spring. We do not know the year or the place it was written. "The old days south of the pond" must be something from his younger years, but the lyric does not say what.

author_note.zh: 程垓，字正伯，号书舟，眉山（今四川眉山）人，南宋词人，生卒年不详。他的词集叫《书舟词》。他的词写离愁和伤春的很多，语言清新自然，感情细腻，读起来像在和人说心里话。
author_note.en: Cheng Gai, also called Zhengbo or Shuzhou, came from Meishan in today's Sichuan. He was a Southern Song lyric poet; his birth and death years are not known. His collection is called "Lyrics of Shuzhou". Many of his lyrics are about parting and the sadness of spring ending. His words are fresh and natural and his feelings delicate, as if he were telling you what is on his mind.

appreciation.zh: 上阕从一夜风雨写起。词人没看见花落，却猜到老家的花已经不多了。他怪自己一年都在发愁，白白辜负了春天。柳树困了，桃花懒了，杏和梅已经结出小果子，春天就这样轻易地走了。接着他转过念头：就算春天永远在，花永远开，人还是会老。真正留不住的，是人自己。下阕回想往事，可是头发白了，越想越难受，只剩下看花的老眼和伤心的眼泪。最后他忽然振作起来：花少了不怕，怕的是人老了就没了兴致。等花开得最热闹的时候，我还要留住云、借来月，痛痛快快醉一场。全词从伤心写到不服老，读来既有叹息，也有一股倔强。
appreciation.en: The first stanza begins with a night of wind and rain. The poet did not see the flowers fall, but he guesses few are left at home. He blames himself for worrying all year and wasting spring. The willows are sleepy, the peach blossoms lazy, and the apricots and plums already have small fruit. Spring has left so easily. Then he turns the thought around: even if spring lasted forever and flowers never stopped blooming, people would still grow old. What truly cannot be kept is ourselves. The second stanza looks back on the past, but his hair is grey and remembering only hurts. All he has are old eyes for flowers and sad tears. At the end he suddenly cheers up. Fewer flowers do not scare him; what scares him is losing his zest in old age. When the flowers are at their liveliest, he will keep the clouds, borrow the moon and get happily drunk. The lyric moves from grief to refusing to give in to age. There is a sigh in it, and also a stubborn spirit.
